cards.prose: The disciples show him the buildings, and this verse is where Yahuah (the LORD) sent a prophet to stand in the temple gate with the same news. Jeremiah's sermon says a house cannot shelter a people who trust it and will not amend their ways: *Trust ye not in lying words, saying, The temple of Yahuah (LORD), The temple of Yahuah (LORD), The temple of Yahuah (LORD), are these.* (Jeremiah 7:4)
cards.member_sentence: Where Jeremiah's temple sermon begins, warning a people who trusted the house of Yahuah (the LORD) while they would not amend their ways.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says no stone will be left on another, and Jeremiah heard the same sentence long before: Yahuah (the LORD) will make the house *like Shiloh*. The reason stands in the verses just ahead of it, *If ye will not hearken to me, to walk in my law, which I have set before you* (Jeremiah 26:4), so the house falls for the law refused, not for the stones.
cards.member_sentence: The house made like Shiloh, said because the people would not hearken to walk in the law set before them.

cards.prose: When Yahusha (Jesus) says the stones will be thrown down, he is saying what the elders in Jeremiah's day remembered Micah saying about Zion. They also remembered how it was met: *did he not fear Yahuah (LORD), and besought Yahuah (LORD), and Yahuah (LORD) repented him of the evil which he had pronounced against them?* (Jeremiah 26:19) The warning was always a call to turn as much as a sentence.
cards.member_phrase: Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest
cards.member_sentence: Micah's sentence on Zion, remembered by the elders in Jeremiah's day, together with the king's turning that held the evil back.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says the temple will be thrown down, and Micah says what made it ready to fall. The heads judged for reward, the priests taught for hire, the prophets divined for money, and every one of them said *Is not Yahuah (LORD) among us? none evil can come upon us.* (Micah 3:11) Zion is plowed *for your sake*, because of what its rulers made of it.
cards.member_phrase: Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps
cards.member_sentence: The rulers who judged for reward and taught for hire yet trusted the house, so Zion would be plowed as a field.

cards.prose: He has just come out of the temple, and the sentence he spoke over it in the chapter before is what the disciples are pointing at: *your house is left unto you desolate*. He says *your house*, and what is left desolate is the temple and the rule that sat over it. The verse after gives the way back, for they will see him again when they say, *Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord).* (Matthew 23:39)
cards.member_sentence: The sentence he spoke over the temple before walking out of it, with the promise in the next verse that they will see him again.

cards.prose: Luke shows the heart behind the sentence. He comes near the city and weeps over it, and the words that follow are the ones the disciples hear as they leave the temple: *And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.* (Luke 19:44) He says it weeping.
cards.member_sentence: He wept over the city before saying that not one stone would be left on another.

cards.prose: Mark sets the scene a little closer. Peter, James, John and Andrew ask him privately, sitting *over against the temple*, with the buildings still in front of them that he said would be thrown down. Matthew says only that *the disciples* came, and Mark names the four who put the question.
cards.member_sentence: Names the four who asked, sitting on the mount of Olives opposite the temple.

cards.prose: In Luke the question comes straight out of the temple talk. He has just said *there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down* (Luke 21:6), and they ask *when shall these things be?* and what sign there will be. It is the same two asks Matthew's disciples make on the mount, here put to him at the temple itself.
cards.member_sentence: Luke's version of the question, when and what sign, asked straight after he says not one stone will be left.

cards.prose: The disciples ask for the sign of *thy coming* while he sits on the mount of Olives, and Zechariah had already marked that hill for the day. The verse before has Yahuah (the LORD) to *go forth, and fight against those nations* (Zechariah 14:3), so the question is asked at the very place the prophet named.
cards.member_phrase: And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east
cards.member_sentence: The mountain where he sits to answer is the one the prophet named as the place his feet stand on the day.

cards.prose: After those who come in his name, Yahusha (Jesus) says wars follow, *nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom* (Matthew 24:7). Isaiah already had that picture for Egypt and says whose hand it is: *I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians*, *city against city, and kingdom against kingdom*. What Matthew calls the beginning of sorrows is strife Yahuah (the LORD) can send among a people, not only a sign to watch for.
cards.member_phrase: And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) sets Egyptian against Egyptian, city against city and kingdom against kingdom, the strife Matthew names among the first sorrows.
cards.flag: Source verse is 24:5 (those who come in his name); the pair answers the wars of 24:7, which I quote with its citation to hold the two verses together.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) puts wars among the first sorrows, *nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom* (Matthew 24:7), and Zechariah shows who stirs that fight when it falls on the nations that came against Jerusalem. *a great tumult from Yahuah (LORD) shall be among them*, and every hand rises against the neighbour's hand.
cards.member_phrase: a great tumult from Yahuah (LORD) shall be among them; and they shall lay hold every one on the hand of his neighbour
cards.member_sentence: A tumult from Yahuah (the LORD) turns the nations against one another, every hand against his neighbour's hand.
cards.flag: Source verse is 24:5; the pair answers the wars of 24:7, quoted with its citation.

cards.prose: He said this to the twelve when he first sent them out, and he says it again on the mountain with the circle widened, *all men* becoming *all nations*. The promise rides with it both times: *he that endureth to the end shall be saved*.
cards.member_sentence: The same hatred for his name and the same promise to the one who endures, first spoken to the twelve when he sent them out.

cards.prose: Matthew says his people will be handed over, killed, and hated for his name. In John it begins in the temple, where those who answer him ask what sign he shows for driving out the sellers: *What sign shewest thou unto us*. His answer is his own death and rising, *Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up* (John 2:19), so the killing foretold for them was first spoken of him.
cards.member_sentence: The first challenge to him, in the temple, which he answers with the sign of his own death and rising.
cards.flag: The old note meant 1 John 2:18 (many antichrists). The pair is the gospel of John, so I wrote to the temple sign question actually on the page and did not re-point.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) opens this talk with *Take heed that no man deceive you* (Matthew 24:4), and Paul begins the same way, *Let no man deceive you by any means*, before he says what must come first, *a falling away first*, and the son of perdition revealed. Matthew shows how a falling away looks from inside: *shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another* (Matthew 24:10).
cards.member_phrase: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition
cards.member_sentence: Paul warns that the day waits on a falling away and the revealing of the son of perdition, opening with the same words as Matthew: let no man deceive you.

cards.prose: Matthew says *And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.* (Matthew 24:12) Paul says that iniquity did not wait for the end to begin: *the mystery of iniquity doth already work*. Iniquity there is lawlessness, and it was already at work in his day, held back until the one who holds it back *be taken out of the way*.
cards.member_sentence: The lawlessness Matthew says will abound was already working in Paul's day, held back until what restrains it is taken out of the way.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says the faithful will be hated and that *the love of many shall wax cold* (Matthew 24:12). Paul gives that season its name, the *last days*, and says what makes the times *perilous*: men *lovers of pleasures more than lovers of Elohim (God)* (2 Timothy 3:4). The danger in both is love turned the wrong way.
cards.member_sentence: Paul names the same season the last days and says what makes it perilous, love of self and pleasure in place of love for Elohim (God).

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says the nations will hate his people for his name, and Isaiah shows what else is true in that same darkness: *the darkness shall cover the earth* (Isaiah 60:2), yet the light has come on Zion. *the Gentiles shall come to thy light* (Isaiah 60:3), and the next verse says who is coming: *thy sons shall come from far* (Isaiah 60:4). The ones who come are the scattered sons and daughters, coming home.
cards.member_sentence: The light risen on Zion in a dark earth, with the Gentiles and the sons from far coming to it.
cards.flag: Isaiah 60:3 keeps the word Gentiles; I read who comes from 60:4 (thy sons from far, thy daughters) as the brief asks.

cards.prose: In Matthew all nations hate his people; in Isaiah all nations and tongues are gathered to see the glory of Yahuah (the LORD), and a sign is set among them. Out of them he sends *those that escape of them unto the nations* (Isaiah 66:19), to the far places that have not heard, and *they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto Yahuah (LORD) out of all nations* (Isaiah 66:20) to his holy mountain.
cards.member_phrase: I will gather all nations and tongues; and they shall come, and see my glory
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) gathers all nations and tongues to see his glory, and sends those who escape out to the far places that have not heard.

cards.prose: Hatred for his name is one thing; carrying his name is another. The ones sent away in the Sermon had prophesied in it, *have we not prophesied in thy name?* (Matthew 7:22), and they are called *ye that work iniquity*. Iniquity there is lawlessness, the Torah set aside, and it is the same word Yahusha (Jesus) uses again in this chapter: *And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.* (Matthew 24:12)
cards.member_sentence: The verdict on those who used his name while setting the law aside: he sends away the workers of lawlessness.
cards.flag: The live thread lord-lord-and-torahlessness is unanchored; assemble496 will need an entry for it in ref/anchors496.json (Matthew 7:21-23 fits).

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) sends the reader to Daniel by name, so here is the verse itself. Daniel says the sacrifice and the oblation are made to cease in the midst of the week, and that *for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate*, until the end that is determined is poured out. Matthew's abomination is set to *stand in the holy place*, the place where that sacrifice was kept.
cards.member_phrase: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate
cards.member_sentence: Daniel's own words for the desolation Matthew names: the sacrifice made to cease and the place made desolate until the end determined.
cards.flag: Joined to the thread anchored on Daniel 9:27 because the target is that thread's own anchor verse; the mirror pair (Daniel 9:27 to Matthew 24:15) already sits there.

cards.prose: A few verses on, Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of a tribulation with no equal, and Daniel gave that trouble its measure first: *a time of trouble*. In Daniel the trouble is not the last word. At that time *thy people shall be delivered*, and the ones named are those *found written in the book*.
cards.member_phrase: there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book
cards.member_sentence: The time of trouble such as never was, with the people delivered, every one found written in the book.

cards.prose: Luke names what the desolation looks like when it arrives: *Jerusalem compassed with armies*. Where Matthew sends the reader to Daniel, Luke tells the disciples what they will see and what it means, *the desolation thereof is nigh*, and the same flight follows in both gospels, those in Judaea to the mountains.
cards.member_sentence: Luke's telling of the same warning: Jerusalem surrounded by armies is the sign that its desolation is near.
cards.flag: Joined to the Luke 21:20-24 thread because the target is that thread's own opening verse.

cards.prose: Matthew has the abomination standing *in the holy place*, and Paul, one verse on, puts a man in the same kind of place: *so that he as Elohim (God) sitteth in the temple of Elohim (God), shewing himself that he is Elohim (God).* (2 Thessalonians 2:4) Both give the sign by where it stands, and Paul too begins by warning that none should be deceived before *a falling away* and the son of perdition.
cards.member_phrase: except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition
cards.member_sentence: Paul says the day waits on a falling away and the revealing of the son of perdition, who then takes his seat in the temple of Elohim (God).

cards.prose: Matthew has the abomination standing in the holy place. In Revelation the angel puts a reed in John's hand and says to measure the temple, the altar and the worshippers, but to leave the outer court, *for it is given unto the Gentiles: and the holy city shall they tread under foot forty and two months* (Revelation 11:2). Revelation counts that time in months; Matthew gives no count.
cards.member_phrase: Rise, and measure the temple of Elohim (God), and the altar, and them that worship therein
cards.member_sentence: A temple measured in Revelation, with the altar and the worshippers counted and the outer court given over.

cards.prose: Matthew gives the sign of the holy place and no number of months. Revelation shows *a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies*, given to the beast the dragon empowered, and *power was given unto him to continue forty and two months*. Revelation counts in months where Matthew counts nothing.
cards.member_sentence: A beast given a mouth for great blasphemies and a set time of forty and two months, counted as Revelation counts it.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) warns that false prophets *shall shew great signs and wonders* (Matthew 24:24), and Moses had already given the test for such a sign. Even when *the sign or the wonder come to pass* (Deuteronomy 13:2), the prophet is refused if he leads away from Yahuah (the LORD), because the sign is the way Yahuah (the LORD) proves whether his people love him, and the standard is *keep his commandments, and obey his voice* (Deuteronomy 13:4).
cards.member_sentence: Opens the Torah's test for a prophet who gives a sign or a wonder: the sign alone proves nothing.

cards.prose: Right after the warning against *Lo, here*, Yahusha (Jesus) says *wheresoever the carcase is, there will the eagles be gathered together* (Matthew 24:28). Job shows the bird: she dwells on the rock and *her eyes behold afar off* (Job 39:29), and *where the slain are, there is she*. Judgment needs no one to point to it; it finds the slain wherever they lie.
cards.member_sentence: The eagle of Job finds the slain wherever they lie, the bird behind Matthew's saying about the carcase and the eagles.
cards.flag: Source verse is 24:23; the old notes in this group point at the eagles of 24:28, which I quote with its citation.

cards.prose: Isaiah has the beasts called in to devour, and the verses after say why the flock is open: *they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain, from his quarter.* (Isaiah 56:11) Matthew has voices saying *Lo, here* and the eagles gathered to the carcase; Isaiah shows the carcase laid out by shepherds who looked to their own gain.
cards.member_sentence: The call to the beasts to devour comes where the watchmen are blind and the shepherds look only to their own gain.

cards.prose: Hosea has an eagle of his own, coming against the house of Yahuah (the LORD), and the reason is in the same breath: they *transgressed my covenant, and trespassed against my law*. When Yahusha (Jesus) says *wheresoever the carcase is, there will the eagles be gathered together* (Matthew 24:28), the carcase is a house that broke the covenant.
cards.member_phrase: He shall come as an eagle against the house of Yahuah (LORD), because they have transgressed my covenant, and trespassed against my law
cards.member_sentence: An eagle comes against the house of Yahuah (the LORD) because the covenant was broken and the law trespassed against.

cards.prose: Matthew says the eagles gather to the carcase; Revelation shows the call that brings the birds, an angel standing in the sun crying to *all the fowls that fly in the midst of heaven* to the supper of the great Elohim (God). Beside Yahusha's (Jesus's) warning about signs and wonders, the verses after show what was gathered against the rider: *the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him* (Revelation 19:20).
cards.member_phrase: Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great Elohim (God)
cards.member_sentence: An angel in the sun summons all the birds of heaven to the supper of the great Elohim (God).

cards.prose: Luke puts the warning in the same order Matthew does. *See here; or, see there: go not after them* comes first, and then at once the lightning, *as the lightning, that lighteneth out of the one part under heaven, shineth unto the other part under heaven; so shall also the Son of Adam be in his day* (Luke 17:24). A coming that fills the sky cannot be pointed at in a room or a desert.
cards.member_sentence: Luke's warning against see here, see there, followed at once by the lightning that fills the whole sky.

cards.prose: Isaiah says the stars *shall not give their light* and the sun is *darkened in his going forth*, and the verse before says whose day it is: *the day of Yahuah (LORD) cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate* (Isaiah 13:9). Yahusha (Jesus) uses the same darkened sun and moon for his coming, so the sky is the sign of the day of Yahuah (the LORD), and that day clears the sinners out of the land.
cards.member_phrase: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine
cards.member_sentence: The darkened sun, moon and stars as the sign of the day of Yahuah (the LORD), when the sinners are cleared out of the land.

cards.prose: Matthew's moon gives no light and the sun is darkened; Isaiah says why they hide, *the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed*, because Yahuah (the LORD) is reigning *in mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, and before his ancients gloriously*. The sky goes dark before a greater light, and the verse before has the host of the high ones and the kings of the earth shut up in the pit to be visited after many days.
cards.member_sentence: The moon confounded and the sun ashamed when Yahuah (the LORD) of hosts reigns in Zion and Jerusalem.

cards.prose: Matthew has the stars falling and the powers of the heavens shaken. Isaiah has the sky itself undone, the heavens *rolled together as a scroll*, and the host dropping *as a falling fig from the fig tree*. Two verses earlier *the indignation of Yahuah (LORD) is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies* (Isaiah 34:2), so the falling sky belongs to a judgment on the nations.
cards.member_phrase: all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree
cards.member_sentence: The host of heaven dissolved and the heavens rolled up like a scroll, in a day of indignation upon the nations.

cards.prose: Joel shows the earth quaking and the heavens trembling, the sun and the moon dark and the stars withdrawing their shining, and then the voice of Yahuah (the LORD) before his army: *the day of Yahuah (LORD) is great and very terrible; and who can abide it?* (Joel 2:11) Inside that same day he says *turn ye even to me with all your heart* (Joel 2:12). The call to turn is spoken in the middle of the darkened sky.
cards.member_sentence: The earth quaking and the sun, moon and stars dark before the army of Yahuah (the LORD), with a call to turn in the same passage.

cards.prose: Joel says the sun is turned to darkness and the moon to blood *before the great and the terrible day*, so the sky is the herald and not the day itself, which is how Matthew puts it too. The verse after says who is delivered: *whosoever shall call on the name of Yahuah (LORD) shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as Yahuah (LORD) hath said, and in the remnant whom Yahuah (LORD) shall call.* (Joel 2:32)
cards.member_sentence: The sun darkened and the moon turned to blood come before the great and terrible day of Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.prose: Joel gives the darkened sun and moon at the turning of the harvest: *Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe* (Joel 3:13), multitudes in the valley of decision, and then the sky goes dark. After it, *Yahuah (LORD) also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shall shake: but Yahuah (LORD) will be the hope of his people* (Joel 3:16).
cards.member_sentence: Joel's darkened sun and moon fall in the valley of decision, where the harvest is ripe and Yahuah (the LORD) is the hope of his people.

cards.prose: Ezekiel's line is almost word for word Matthew's *the moon shall not give her light*, and it is spoken of the fall of Pharaoh, when Yahuah (the LORD) covers the heaven over him: *All the bright lights of heaven will I make dark over thee* (Ezekiel 32:8). The darkened sky is how the prophets speak when a proud power comes down, and Matthew sets it over the whole earth at his coming.
cards.member_phrase: I will cover the heaven, and make the stars thereof dark; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light
cards.member_sentence: Almost Matthew's words, said against Pharaoh when Yahuah (the LORD) puts him out: the sky is covered over a proud power's fall.

cards.prose: Amos has the sun going down at noon and Yahuah (the LORD) darkening the earth *in the clear day*. The verses after say what that day does to a people at ease: *I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation* (Amos 8:10), and then a famine, *not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of Yahuah (LORD)* (Amos 8:11). The darkness in the sky has a darkness in hearing to match.
cards.member_phrase: I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day
cards.member_sentence: The sun going down at noon on the day of Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), with feasts turned to mourning and a famine of hearing his word to follow.

cards.prose: Micah turns the picture on the false prophets: night to them, no vision, *the day shall be dark over them*, and in the end *there is no answer of Elohim (God)* (Micah 3:7). The sun going down over them is a judgment on those who spoke for him falsely, and Matthew's darkened sun comes in a chapter that warns again and again of false prophets.
cards.member_phrase: the sun shall go down over the prophets, and the day shall be dark over them
cards.member_sentence: The sun goes down over the prophets who make his people err: no vision, no answer, the day dark over them.

cards.prose: Zephaniah names the day the darkness belongs to: *The great day of Yahuah (LORD) is near*, and he describes it, *a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness* (Zephaniah 1:15). Matthew puts the sun's darkening and the Son of Adam in the clouds in the same hour, and Zephaniah's day already has darkness and clouds in it.
cards.member_phrase: The great day of Yahuah (LORD) is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly
cards.member_sentence: The great day of Yahuah (the LORD) is near and hastening, the day whose darkness and clouds Matthew's sky signs belong to.

cards.prose: Revelation opens the sixth seal and shows the same sky: the sun goes black and the moon turns to blood, and then *the stars of heaven fell unto the earth, even as a fig tree casteth her untimely figs* (Revelation 6:13). Matthew's sun, moon and stars are the same three, told in this book's own words, with an earthquake and kings hiding in the rocks.
cards.member_phrase: there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became as blood
cards.member_sentence: At the sixth seal an earthquake, the sun black as sackcloth and the moon as blood, as Revelation tells the darkened sky.

cards.prose: Revelation has the darkening too, but by measure: at the fourth trumpet a third part of the sun, the moon and the stars is smitten, and day and night each lose a third. Matthew gives no fraction, and Revelation keeps its own count of trumpets; the next verse is an angel crying *Woe, woe, woe, to the inhabiters of the earth* (Revelation 8:13) for the trumpets still to sound.
cards.member_phrase: the third part of the sun was smitten, and the third part of the moon, and the third part of the stars
cards.member_sentence: At the fourth trumpet a third of the sun, moon and stars is struck, a darkening Revelation counts by parts.

cards.prose: Peter reads Joel to the men of Yashar'el (Israel) and keeps the sky signs in the reading: *The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before that great and notable day of Yahuah (Lord) come* (Acts 2:20). The darkened sun Matthew sets after the tribulation was already known to the apostles as what comes before the great day, a day still ahead of them.
cards.member_sentence: Peter's quotation of Joel includes the wonders in heaven and signs on earth that come before the great day of Yahuah (the Lord).

cards.prose: Matthew has the Son of Adam coming on the clouds, and Daniel is the vision behind it: a figure *like* the Son of Adam, brought near before the Ancient of days. Daniel's word is *like*, for the one who comes took on flesh and looked like a son of Adam, and Daniel says what is given him: *dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him* (Daniel 7:14). Yahusha (Jesus) takes that figure as himself.
cards.member_phrase: one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days
cards.member_sentence: The vision behind Matthew's saying: one like the Son of Adam comes with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of days.

cards.prose: Matthew has the tribes mourn when they see the Son of Adam coming. Zechariah says why: the house of David look on the one they pierced, and the mourning goes through the families one by one, *the land shall mourn, every family apart* (Zechariah 12:12). The one the tribes see in the clouds is the one they pierced.
cards.member_phrase: they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son
cards.member_sentence: They look on him they pierced and mourn as for an only son, the mourning Matthew says all the tribes will make.

cards.prose: Revelation opens with the same sight in the same order: *he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him*, and then the mourning, *all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him*, where Matthew has *all the tribes of the earth mourn*. John also names who is among those who see, *they also which pierced him*, and two verses on the speaker gives his own name: *which is, and which was, and which is to come* (Revelation 1:8).
cards.member_sentence: John's opening gives the cloud, the sight of every eye including those who pierced him, and the wailing of all kindreds.

cards.prose: In Revelation the one on the cloud is seen *like unto the Son of Adam*, a golden crown on his head and *a sharp sickle* in his hand, and an angel comes out of the temple to cry *for the time is come for thee to reap; for the harvest of the earth is ripe* (Revelation 14:15). Matthew's Son of Adam on the clouds sends angels to gather; Revelation's rider holds the sickle himself, and the earth is reaped.
cards.member_phrase: upon the cloud one sat like unto the Son of Adam, having on his head a golden crown, and in his hand a sharp sickle
cards.member_sentence: A white cloud and one seated on it like unto the Son of Adam, with a golden crown and a sharp sickle for the ripe harvest.

cards.prose: Revelation shows him coming another way: heaven opened, a white horse, a rider called *Faithful and True* who judges and makes war *in righteousness*, and whose name the next verses give as *The Word of Elohim (God)* (Revelation 19:13). Matthew's coming is in the clouds with a trumpet; this is another book's picture of his coming, a rider where Matthew has a cloud.
cards.member_phrase: he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war
cards.member_sentence: Heaven opened and a rider on a white horse, called Faithful and True, judging and making war in righteousness.

cards.prose: Matthew has the Son of Adam coming in the clouds, and the psalm says whose road the cloud is. Yahuah (the LORD) my Elohim (God) *maketh the clouds his chariot*, and *walketh upon the wings of the wind*. The one who rides the clouds in scripture is Yahuah (the LORD), and Yahusha (Jesus) puts his own coming there.
cards.member_sentence: The clouds are the chariot of Yahuah (the LORD), who walks upon the wings of the wind.

cards.prose: Isaiah says Yahuah (the LORD) *rideth upon a swift cloud*, and the idols of Egypt tremble before him. Matthew sets the Son of Adam on the clouds of heaven in the same kind of coming, with the tribes mourning at the sight. The cloud brings him to judge.
cards.member_phrase: Behold, Yahuah (LORD) rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) rides a swift cloud to come in judgment, and the idols move at his presence.

cards.prose: In Nahum the clouds are *the dust of his feet*, so the sky is only the road Yahuah (the LORD) walks. He comes with *his way in the whirlwind and in the storm*, and the same verse says he *will not at all acquit the wicked*. When Yahusha (Jesus) places the Son of Adam on the clouds, he sets his coming on that road.
cards.member_phrase: Yahuah (LORD) hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet
cards.member_sentence: The clouds are the dust of the feet of Yahuah (the LORD), who goes his way in the whirlwind and will not acquit the wicked.

cards.prose: Moses told Yashar'el (Israel) that no one is too far to be fetched: even *the outmost parts of heaven* will not keep Yahuah (the LORD) from gathering his own. Matthew's *from one end of heaven to the other* is that reach, and the gathering follows the return, *shalt return unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day* (Deuteronomy 30:2).
cards.member_sentence: No one driven to the outmost parts of heaven is out of reach: Yahuah (the LORD) gathers and fetches his own from there.

cards.prose: Isaiah calls it a recovery *the second time*, and the next verse says who and from where: Yahuah (the LORD) *shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth* (Isaiah 11:12). Matthew's elect from the four winds are those, both houses, brought back.
cards.member_phrase: Yahuah (Lord) shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left
cards.member_sentence: The second time Yahuah (the LORD) sets his hand to recover the remnant of his people from Assyria, Egypt and the islands of the sea.

cards.prose: Isaiah has the same trumpet, *the great trumpet*, and says who comes at the sound: those *ready to perish in the land of Assyria*, and the outcasts of Egypt. The verse before has them *gathered one by one, O ye children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Isaiah 27:12). Matthew's great sound of a trumpet is that call, and it brings the outcasts to worship at Jerusalem.
cards.member_phrase: the great trumpet shall be blown, and they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt
cards.member_sentence: The great trumpet blown in that day, and the outcasts of Assyria and Egypt coming to worship Yahuah (the LORD) at Jerusalem.

cards.prose: Isaiah names the four winds as directions, east and west here and then north and south: *I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth* (Isaiah 43:6). Those gathered are *thy seed*, sons and daughters, *every one that is called by my name* (Isaiah 43:7).
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) brings the seed of Yashar'el (Israel) from the east and gathers them from the west, with the north and south to follow.

cards.prose: Isaiah names the one who gathers by what he does: he *gathereth the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel)*, and then adds *others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him*. It is one gathering, the outcasts first and then more of the scattered brought in beside them, and Matthew's elect from the four winds are those outcasts. The others are not a different people joined to them.
cards.member_phrase: which gathereth the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel) saith, Yet will I gather others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him
cards.member_sentence: He who gathers the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel) will gather others beside those already gathered, still the one scattered people.

cards.prose: Where Matthew sends angels to the four winds, Jeremiah sends the gathering first to the north country and then to *the coasts of the earth*, and the company that returns is not picked over: *the blind and the lame, the woman with child*, a great company. The next verses give the reason, *for I am a father to Yashar'el (Israel), and Ephraim is my firstborn* (Jeremiah 31:9).
cards.member_phrase: I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame, the woman with child and her that travaileth with child together: a great company shall return thither
cards.member_sentence: A great company, even the blind, the lame and women with child, brought back from the north country and the coasts of the earth.

cards.prose: Ezekiel's *on every side* is Matthew's four winds: Yahuah (the Lord GOD) takes the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from where they have gone and brings them to their own land. The verses after say what they become, *I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezekiel 37:22), with one shepherd over them, a people who *walk in my judgments, and observe my statutes, and do them* (Ezekiel 37:24).
cards.member_phrase: I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the Lord GOD) takes the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from where they have gone and gathers them on every side into their own land.

cards.prose: The trumpet in Matthew has an old home in the appointed times. Yahuah (the LORD) told Moses that the first day of the seventh month is *a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation* (Leviticus 23:24), a calling together of the assembly by trumpet. The great sound of a trumpet that gathers the elect in Matthew sounds the call the Torah already set for his people.
cards.member_sentence: The verse that opens the appointed time of the trumpets, spoken by Yahuah (the LORD) to Moses.

cards.prose: Numbers gives the same day in its own words and calls it *a day of blowing the trumpets unto you*, an holy convocation on the first day of the seventh month. A convocation is a calling together, and Matthew's trumpet calls the elect together from every quarter; the day the Torah set aside for trumpets already carried that picture.
cards.member_phrase: ye shall have an holy convocation; ye shall do no servile work: it is a day of blowing the trumpets unto you
cards.member_sentence: The first day of the seventh month is an holy convocation, a day of blowing the trumpets.

cards.prose: Paul comforts those grieving *them which are asleep*: the hope is that *the dead in Messiah (Christ) shall rise first* (1 Thessalonians 4:16) at his coming, at the trump of Elohim (God), the same coming in which Matthew's great trumpet gathers the scattered elect. The catching up he names after it, *Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds* (1 Thessalonians 4:17), is a later thing, afterward, and the gathering of the elect is not it.
cards.member_phrase: concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope
cards.member_sentence: Paul's comfort for those grieving the ones who sleep: they are not without hope, because the dead in Messiah (Christ) rise at his coming.
cards.flag: The old note put the catching-up of 1 Thessalonians 4:17 after the reign. Per the brief I wrote only the sleeping dead and their rising, and did not equate Matthew 24:31 with being caught up.

cards.prose: Paul calls it a mystery that *we shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed*, and the verse after says when: *at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed* (1 Corinthians 15:52). Matthew has a great trumpet at his coming; Paul has the dead raised and the living changed at a trumpet.
cards.member_sentence: Paul's mystery that not all will sleep but all will be changed, at the sounding of a trumpet.
cards.flag: The old note carried a two-trumpets claim (this last trump placed at the seventh trumpet after the reign). The brief asks for the change at his coming and no more, so I left that out.

cards.prose: Matthew's *four winds* are held in Revelation by four angels at the corners of the earth, and another angel cries that they must wait *till we have sealed the servants of our Elohim (God) in their foreheads* (Revelation 7:3). The sealed are counted: *an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Revelation 7:4).
cards.member_phrase: four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree
cards.member_sentence: Four angels hold the four winds of the earth until the servants of Elohim (God) are sealed, a hundred forty and four thousand of the tribes.

cards.prose: The sealed of the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) are seen again here with the Lamb on mount Zion, *having his Father's name written in their foreheads*, the seal they were given. Where Matthew's angels gather the elect from the four winds, Revelation shows the company standing together on Zion, *redeemed from among men, being the firstfruits unto Elohim (God) and to the Lamb* (Revelation 14:4).
cards.member_phrase: a Lamb stood on the mount Zion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads
cards.member_sentence: A hundred forty and four thousand stand with the Lamb on mount Zion, with his Father's name written in their foreheads.

cards.prose: The fig tree tells the season, and the verse after it says what outlasts the season: *Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.* (Matthew 24:35) He measured his words the same way on the mountain where he taught, heaven and earth going before *one jot or one tittle* goes from the law. The words that will not pass are the law's own, so nothing in the Olivet talk reads as the commandments ending.
cards.member_sentence: Heaven and earth pass before one jot or tittle passes from the law, the same measure he gives his words in Matthew 24.
cards.flag: Source verse is 24:32 (the fig tree); the old notes in this group all carry the point of 24:35, so I quote 24:35 with its citation to hold the pairs together.

cards.prose: Mark gives the fig tree the same close, with his words outlasting heaven and earth, and runs it straight into the hidden hour: *But of that day and that hour knoweth no man* (Mark 13:32). The sign you can read in the leaves and the day nobody can name sit side by side, with his words standing over both.
cards.member_sentence: Mark's parallel to the saying that heaven and earth pass but his words do not, set right before the word about the hidden day and hour.

cards.prose: The psalm says of the heavens and earth what Matthew says: they are made things and they pass. *They shall perish, but thou shalt endure: yea, all of them shall wax old like a garment* (Psalm 102:26). The one addressed laid the foundation of the earth *of old*, and when Yahusha (Jesus) sets his words against the passing of heaven and earth, he puts them on the side of what endures.
cards.member_sentence: The heavens are the work of his hands and they will perish, but he endures, the measure Matthew gives his own words.

cards.prose: Matthew's *my words shall not pass away* (Matthew 24:35) is Isaiah's line in the first person: *the word of our Elohim (God) shall stand for ever*. Yahusha (Jesus) calls that word his own. Further down the same chapter the one who comes feeds his flock and gathers the lambs: *He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm* (Isaiah 40:11).
cards.member_sentence: The grass withers and the flower fades but the word of our Elohim (God) stands for ever, the line Matthew's saying echoes.

cards.prose: Isaiah sets the passing of heaven and earth against what does not pass: the heavens *vanish away like smoke*, the earth *wax old like a garment*, but *my righteousness shall not be abolished*. The verse after says who is listening, *the people in whose heart is my law* (Isaiah 51:7), so what is not abolished is tied to the law in the heart.
cards.member_phrase: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath: for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner: but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished
cards.member_sentence: The heavens vanish like smoke and the earth wears out like a garment, but his salvation and his righteousness are not abolished.

cards.prose: Twice in Matthew the one who is Elohim (God) points past himself to the Father. At the cup the seats at his right and left are not his to give but the Father's to prepare, and here the day and hour are known to the Father only. He does not lose what he is by saying so; the Son stands under the Father and says it plainly.
cards.member_phrase: to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father
cards.member_sentence: The seats at his right and left are not his to give but the Father's, the same deference he shows about the day and hour.

cards.prose: Mark names the Son himself among those who do not know the day: not man, not the angels, *neither the Son, but the Father*. Matthew's *but my Father only* says the same from the other side. The Son who is Elohim (God) stands under the Father's timing and says so.
cards.member_sentence: Mark adds that neither the Son knows the day and hour, but the Father only, the parallel to Matthew 24:36.
cards.flag: Joined to the Mark 13:32 thread because the target is that thread's own anchor verse.

cards.prose: After the resurrection the disciples ask the question they asked on the mount in its plainest form: *restore again the kingdom to Yashar'el (Israel)?* He does not say there will be no restoring. He says the times are *which the Father hath put in his own power* (Acts 1:7), and Matthew's *my Father only* is the same answer.
cards.member_phrase: they asked of him, saying, Adonai (Lord), wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Yashar'el (Israel)?
cards.member_sentence: The disciples ask whether he will now restore the kingdom to Yashar'el (Israel), and the answer is that the time is the Father's.

cards.prose: Matthew shows the Son holding the day back to the Father; the psalm shows the same order in a picture. David's *my Lord* sits at the right hand of Yahuah (the LORD) *until* the Father makes his enemies the footstool, so the one at the right hand waits on the Father for the day.
cards.member_sentence: The one David calls my Adonai (Lord) sits at the right hand of Yahuah (the LORD) until his enemies are made his footstool.

cards.prose: Matthew names marrying and giving in marriage as the mark of the days of Noah, and Genesis shows what marriage had become: *the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.* (Genesis 6:2) The days Yahusha (Jesus) points to began with that crossing, so the days of Noah are more than eating and drinking.
cards.member_sentence: The days of Noah begin when men multiply and the sons of Elohim (God) take the daughters of men as wives.

cards.prose: Matthew has Noah going into the ark and the rest knowing nothing until the flood took them. Genesis gives Noah's side: Yahuah (the LORD) calls him and his house in because *thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation*. One household was called in while the world went on eating and marrying, and the flood that *took them all away* (Matthew 24:39) was judgment on the rest.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) calls Noah and all his house into the ark because he has seen him righteous in that generation.

cards.prose: Peter sets Noah beside the angels that sinned: Elohim (God) *spared not the angels that sinned* (2 Peter 2:4) and *spared not the old world*, bringing the flood on the ungodly, and saved Noah as *a preacher of righteousness*. In Matthew the people ate and married and knew nothing, while the preacher was building the ark.
cards.member_sentence: Elohim (God) spared not the old world but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, when the flood came on the ungodly.

cards.prose: Matthew says they *knew not until the flood came* (Matthew 24:39), and Peter says the scoffers of the last days walk after their own lusts and ask *Where is the promise of his coming?* (2 Peter 3:4), since all things go on as they were. He answers from the flood: *the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished* (2 Peter 3:6). Those who say nothing will change are Noah's world over again.
cards.member_sentence: Scoffers in the last days walk after their own lusts and say all things continue, as Noah's world did before the flood.
cards.flag: Mapped to a day-and-hour sub-slug, but 2 Peter 3:3-6 turns on the flood, so I placed it in the Noah thread anchored on 24:37-39.

cards.prose: Luke has the same saying and carries the picture further: *They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.* (Luke 17:27) Then comes Lot, and *the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven* (Luke 17:29). Flood and fire both take the unwatching, and in both the household is brought out first.
cards.member_sentence: Luke's parallel: as it was in the days of Noah, so shall it be in the days of the Son of Adam.

cards.prose: In Luke the disciples ask where, and the answer is not a rescue: *Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together.* (Luke 17:37) So the ones taken in Luke are taken to where the carcase lies, which agrees with Matthew, where the flood *took them all away* (Matthew 24:39) and then *the one shall be taken, and the other left*.
cards.member_phrase: in that night there shall be two men in one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left
cards.member_sentence: Luke has two in one bed, one taken and one left, and his answer to where they are taken is the carcase and the eagles.

cards.prose: The order is the text's: *first the tares*, bound and burned, and then the wheat gathered into the barn. So *the one shall be taken, and the other left* cannot be the righteous lifted away and the wicked left behind. In Noah's day those taken were the ones the flood took away; the tares go first, and the wheat is gathered after.
cards.member_phrase: Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn
cards.member_sentence: At the harvest the tares are gathered first and bound to burn, and only then is the wheat gathered into the barn.

cards.prose: Here the Son of Adam sends his angels, as in Matthew 24, and what they gather first is *all things that offend, and them which do iniquity*. Iniquity is lawlessness again. The ones taken in the field and at the mill are such as these, gathered out by the angels, and the ones left are still in the field when the tares are gone.
cards.member_sentence: The Son of Adam's angels gather out of his kingdom all things that offend and them which do iniquity, to be cast into the furnace.

cards.prose: The net is the same lesson: it *gathered of every kind*, and the sorting comes at the shore, where *the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just* (Matthew 13:49). The two in the field and the two at the mill are such a sorting, and the wicked are the ones taken out from among the just, not the just lifted out of the world.
cards.member_sentence: The net gathers every kind and at the end the angels sever the wicked from among the just.

cards.prose: Matthew says *ye know not what hour*; Paul says he does not need to write about *the times and the seasons*, because *yourselves know perfectly that the day of Yahuah (Lord) so cometh as a thief in the night* (1 Thessalonians 5:2). It falls on those who say *Peace and safety* (1 Thessalonians 5:3), but *ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief* (1 Thessalonians 5:4).
cards.member_sentence: Paul says the times and seasons need no writing, for the day comes as a thief, and the verses after tell who it overtakes.

cards.prose: Revelation puts the thief in his own mouth, to the assembly in Sardis, who had *a name that thou livest, and art dead* (Revelation 3:1). The reason for the watching is given: *hold fast, and repent*, or he comes as a thief and they will not know the hour. Even there he finds *a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments* (Revelation 3:4).
cards.member_phrase: Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee
cards.member_sentence: He warns Sardis to watch or he will come as a thief, and notes a few names there who have not defiled their garments.

cards.prose: The thief saying is dropped into the middle of the gathering for battle, *the battle of that great day of El Shaddai (God Almighty)* (Revelation 16:14), and the blessing is on *he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments*. Matthew's household that watches is Revelation's man who keeps his garments, and the one who does not stands naked with his shame seen.
cards.member_sentence: He comes as a thief, and the blessing is on the one who watches and keeps his garments.

cards.prose: Peter gives the thief the full weight of the day: *as a thief in the night*, and what is in it burns. The verse before explains the delay: *Yahuah (Lord) is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness* (2 Peter 3:9). The master's delay is not neglect, and the evil servant in Matthew who says it will not come is counting wrongly.
cards.member_phrase: But the day of Yahuah (Lord) will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up
cards.member_sentence: The day of Yahuah (the Lord) comes as a thief in the night, and the earth and its works are burned up in it.

cards.prose: The next parable opens the same way as the faithful servant's: a master goes away and puts his goods into his servants' hands. In Matthew 24 the goods are the household's meat in due season; in Matthew 25 they are talents. Both ask what each servant did with what was delivered to him while the master was gone.
cards.member_sentence: The same stewardship in the next scene: a man travels, delivers his goods to his servants, and the question is what each did with them.

cards.prose: Luke puts the same servant after the thief and the hour *when ye think not* (Luke 12:40), and has Peter ask whether the parable is for the twelve or for all. Yahusha (Jesus) answers with the steward set over a household. Matthew's *faithful and wise servant* is Luke's *faithful and wise steward*, the one given the household's portion in season.
cards.member_sentence: Luke's parallel: the faithful and wise steward set over the household to give them their portion of meat in due season.

cards.prose: Two household parables of the same shape: a master leaves for a far country and puts others in charge of what is his, then comes to see what was done. In chapter 21 the husbandmen are the rulers of the house, and they killed the servants sent for the fruit; in this chapter the servant over the household is tested the same way, by whether he feeds it or *begin to smite his fellowservants* (Matthew 24:49).
cards.member_phrase: Hear another parable: There was a certain householder, which planted a vineyard, and hedged it round about, and digged a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country
cards.member_sentence: A householder lets his vineyard to husbandmen and goes into a far country, the same leaving and returning that tests the servant.

cards.prose: The word that comes in Ezekiel 34 is the question of this verse asked of the shepherds of Yashar'el (Israel): *should not the shepherds feed the flocks?* (Ezekiel 34:2) A servant set over the household is to give them meat in due season, and the shepherds in Ezekiel feed themselves and not the flock.
cards.member_sentence: The word of Yahuah (the LORD) against the shepherds who feed themselves, the flock unfed.

cards.prose: The evil servant in Matthew beats his fellow servants; Jeremiah has the pastors who *destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture*. Yahuah (the LORD) answers that he will *visit upon you the evil of your doings* (Jeremiah 23:2), and will himself *gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries* (Jeremiah 23:3). Bad stewards scatter the flock, and the master gathers it.
cards.member_sentence: Woe to the pastors who destroy and scatter the sheep of his pasture.

new_threads.title: The temple torn down, and the disciples' question on the mount of Olives
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. A house that bears the name of Yahuah (the LORD) has been told before that it can be taken down, and the line Yahusha (Jesus) speaks as he leaves the temple is the same one the prophets spoke at its gate: *There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.* (Matthew 24:2)

Jeremiah gave Shiloh as the pattern: *Then will I make this house like Shiloh, and will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.* (Jeremiah 26:6) Micah says it of the hill itself: *Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest.* (Micah 3:12) In both places the fall is tied to what the people did, and Yahusha (Jesus) has just said the same: *Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.* (Matthew 23:38)

He does not say it dry-eyed. *And when he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it,* (Luke 19:41) and then he goes out and sits on the mount of Olives, the hill Zechariah named long before. There the disciples come to him alone with the question that the rest of the chapter answers: *Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?* (Matthew 24:3) Mark and Luke carry the same question, so all three Gospels open the talk with a house falling and a hill where he sits.

new_threads.title: The beginning of sorrows: deception, wars, hatred, and the witness to all nations
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. The first sorrows are the old ones, and the first word is a warning: *Take heed that no man deceive you.* (Matthew 24:4) Isaiah had already heard Yahuah (the LORD) say of Egypt, *And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.* (Isaiah 19:2) Yahusha (Jesus) says it of the whole age: *For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places.* (Matthew 24:7) He names them a start, not a finish: *All these are the beginning of sorrows.* (Matthew 24:8)

Hatred comes with them, and so does a call to stand: *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.* (Matthew 10:22) Inside the house the cost is quieter: *And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.* (Matthew 24:12) Iniquity is lawlessness, the Torah set aside, and love going cold is what it does to a people.

Paul writes the same watch to the assembly: *Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;* (2 Thessalonians 2:3) And the sorrows carry a witness with them: *And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.* (Matthew 24:14) Isaiah says where that witness is heading: *it shall come, that I will gather all nations and tongues; and they shall come, and see my glory.* (Isaiah 66:18)

new_threads.title: The abomination of desolation and the great tribulation
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. Yahusha (Jesus) sends the reader back to a named book: *When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)* (Matthew 24:15) The book itself says: *And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined shall be poured upon the desolate.* (Daniel 9:27) The distress he names is Daniel's too: *And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.* (Daniel 12:1) Matthew says it in his own words: *For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be.* (Matthew 24:21)

Paul keeps the same watch in his own letter and stays in it: *Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;* (2 Thessalonians 2:3)

In Revelation John is given a reed and told, *Rise, and measure the temple of Elohim (God), and the altar, and them that worship therein.* (Revelation 11:1) And of the beast, *there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and power was given unto him to continue forty and two months.* (Revelation 13:5)

new_threads.title: False Christs and false prophets, the lightning, and the eagles
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. A sign or a wonder is no proof, and Moses said so first: *If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder,* (Deuteronomy 13:1) and the verses that follow ask whether he turns you from the commandments. Yahusha (Jesus) says it again: *For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.* (Matthew 24:24) He tells them how not to be led: *And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them.* (Luke 17:23)

His own coming needs no pointing out: *For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:27)

The eagles follow it: *For wheresoever the carcase is, there will the eagles be gathered together.* (Matthew 24:28) Job's picture is plain, *Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.* (Job 39:30) and Hosea puts the eagle on the house that broke covenant: *Set the trumpet to thy mouth. He shall come as an eagle against the house of Yahuah (LORD), because they have transgressed my covenant, and trespassed against my law.* (Hosea 8:1) Revelation has a supper of its own: *Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great Elohim (God);* (Revelation 19:17)

new_threads.title: Heaven and earth pass, but his words do not
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. The fig tree gives the season: *Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh:* (Matthew 24:32) The verse that closes the thought gives the measure: *Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.* (Matthew 24:35)

He used the same measure on the mountain where he taught: *For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.* (Matthew 5:18) The words that outlast heaven and earth are tied to the law. Mark carries the saying word for word: *Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.* (Mark 13:31)

The prophets already set the made things against the word. *The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our Elohim (God) shall stand for ever.* (Isaiah 40:8) *Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath: for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner: but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished.* (Isaiah 51:6) The psalm says the heavens are made: *Of old hast thou laid the foundation of the earth: and the heavens are the work of thy hands.* (Psalm 102:25) What he made passes, and the word he spoke does not.

new_threads.title: The day and hour, the taken and the left, and the thief
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. The hour is the Father's: *But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.* (Matthew 24:36) Mark names the Son in it: *But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.* (Mark 13:32) The Son submits to the Father's timing, and the disciples had asked it after the resurrection: *Adonai (Lord), wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Yashar'el (Israel)?* (Acts 1:6) The psalm shows the same order: *Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.* (Psalm 110:1)

Noah's day sets who is taken: *And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:39) Then, *Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.* (Matthew 24:40) The harvest answers the order: *Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn.* (Matthew 13:30) The tares go first, and Luke has the same two in one bed: *the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.* (Luke 17:34)

The watch is the household's: *But know this, that if the goodman of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up.* (Matthew 24:43) Paul says, *But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you.* (1 Thessalonians 5:1) Peter says, *But the day of Yahuah (Lord) will come as a thief in the night.* (2 Peter 3:10) And in Revelation, *Behold, I come as a thief. Blessed is he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame.* (Revelation 16:15)
